title: Ledger capacity boundary: at cap, all-sensitive overflow evicts the OLDEST observation — identity tracking for it degrades, label containment persists
note: Eviction semantics probe (drives the published RunPolicyGateway API directly, no model). 600 sensitive observations against the default 512-entry cap: observation 0 is evicted, so a verbatim secret-value-0 sink call no longer trips the IDENTITY rule, while the newest observation still does — and BOTH remain denied by the LABEL rule. Documents the honest ceiling: identity tracking is bounded-memory; label-based containment is what persists. It must not be extrapolated into unbounded-run taint integrity.
